nodes.question: Is the mug referred to in the instruction visibly positioned to the right of the headphones in the edited image?
nodes.criteria: pass: The edited image establishes the requested mug to the right of the headphones. fail: The requested mug is identifiable and visibly not to their right, or clear correspondence evidence establishes that a right-side mug is a different object and the requested mug was not placed there. unknown: The target mug's correspondence or final relative position cannot be established. The mere presence of some mug on the right is insufficient when competing candidates make correspondence ambiguous.
nodes.binding: Inspect the final placement independently, using the source image to identify the instruction's mug: the large light-blue handled mug initially left of the black headphones. Assess correspondence using available appearance, shape, scene structure, and positional evidence; do not demand exact preservation of color or size as an additional requirement. Compare against the headphones in the edited scene, accounting for framing changes. Do not assume either that the pale right-side mug is the target or that the blue blur proves the target remained left.

nodes.question: Does comparison of the source and edited images establish any progress in the requested relocation of the source mug to the headphones' right?
nodes.criteria: pass: Visual evidence establishes progress in relocating the requested mug to the headphones' right, whether incomplete or complete. Describe the concrete relocation evidence and whether it establishes incompleteness. fail: Visual evidence establishes no requested relocation progress. unknown: Correspondence, placement, or comparison evidence is insufficient to distinguish progress from no progress. A different mug added on the right, arbitrary movement, disappearance, blur, or other alteration alone does not establish requested progress.
nodes.binding: Compare both images for the relocation of the source light-blue handled mug, not any interchangeable mug-like object. Account for changes in framing, scale, and the headphones' location rather than comparing raw pixel coordinates. Consider all visible evidence of the requested relocation; do not require a specific movement trajectory or exact appearance preservation. Explain whether the evidence shows a genuinely advanced requested placement, no advancement, or an unresolved edit. Inspect independently of s1.

nodes.question: Move the mug so that it is positioned to the right of the headphones.
nodes.criteria: Apply the original instruction and rubric using the support evidence, not a count of passes. Return complete when s1 establishes that the requested mug is to the headphones' right; s2 unknown or skipped does not block this endpoint. Return partial when evidence establishes requested relocation progress and that fulfillment remains incomplete. A passing s2 with a failing s1 can establish partial; if s1 is unknown or skipped, partial requires the available evidence itself to establish both progress and incompleteness. Return absent only when evidence establishes no requested progress and does not establish completion. A failing s1 alone does not establish absence of progress. If endpoint correspondence is unresolved and progress or incompleteness is also unresolved, return unknown. Unknown or skipped supports supply no negative facts. A different added mug, blur, disappearance, or unrelated alterations alone do not earn progress. Resolve contradictory observations only when their concrete evidence supports a consistent interpretation; otherwise remain unknown.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. You receive no reference label or optimization feedback. Return status, evidence, reported confidence (0..1 or null), and used_dependency_ids naming every supplied context check_id exactly once in saved order.
Supports receive source and edited images. Answer only the saved proposition using its binding and criteria. Use pass/fail/unknown. Context is advisory unless listed in required_dependencies. A negative context observation is usable evidence. Unknown, skipped, or invalid context is not a failure and must not stop an independent image inspection. Inspect the images yourself; do not repeat a parent's answer. Return unknown when the relevant fact cannot be established. Confidence reports confidence in this answer, not calibrated correctness.
Fulfillment receives NO images. Use only saved support evidence, original instruction/rubric and frozen composition criteria. Return complete/partial/absent/unknown. Supporting passes answer specific propositions, not a count of completed edits. Their polarity can differ. Apply saved alternatives: optional uncertainty need not prevent a known outcome, but a required unresolved fact makes that outcome unresolved. Never invent a visual fact or convert missing evidence into failure. A conditional skip is not non-applicability. All applicable requested outcomes complete gives yes; no requested progress gives no; known progress short of completion gives partial. Unrelated changes are not progress.
